title: Comparison grid: article and poem
subject: English
unit: Summer 1: Poetry: voice, hope and identity
source: Written for english/y8 lesson 50 (Comparison grid: article and poem (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 50: Non-fiction: whose stories get told?. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

blocks.h: Mary Seacole: facts from the article

timeline.text: Offers to nurse in the Crimean War; turned down
Travels at her own expense; opens the British Hotel near Balaklava
A statue in her honour is unveiled at St Thomas' Hospital

panels.title: The writer's viewpoint
points: Seacole was famous in her lifetime
Then she was largely forgotten for a century

keywords.def: what a writer thinks about a topic
find again something that was lost or forgotten

questions.q: Retrieve: why did Seacole travel to Crimea at her own expense?
questions.a: Because her offer to nurse was turned down, but she was determined to help the soldiers.

questions.q: Find one opinion word in the article and explain it
questions.a: For example: 'forgot' suggests history was careless, not that she did nothing.

questions.q: Core: in the portal response box, write a PEEDL paragraph: 'Compare how the poem and the article present forgotten history.' Starter: 'Both texts argue that..., but...'
questions.a: A PEEDL paragraph: both argue history left people out; the poem through personal anger and dialect, the article through facts and a calm tone.

questions.q: Extend: complete the comparison grid (purpose, tone, method)
questions.a: Purpose: protest / inform and argue. Tone: angry and proud / calm. Method: dialect, repetition / dates, facts.

questions.q: Stretch: suggest one other person who should be better known and why
questions.a: A named figure with a reason and a source.

questions.q: What is the writer's main purpose?
options: to entertain with a made-up story
to argue that forgotten figures deserve a place in history
questions.a: B) to argue that forgotten figures deserve a place in history. The article informs and argues: Seacole's story makes history fuller.

questions.q: Mary Seacole opened the British Hotel near...
Answer the ponder: can history be true but incomplete?
questions.a: For example: yes; accurate facts can still leave voices out.
